subject: Incident synthesis: P95 surge + routing exception — stability checkpoint

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>, SRE Team <sre-team@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-21T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: [ALERT] P95 spike + throughput degradation observed 08:40 PDT

Quick summary: observed a sustained P95 token latency jump (~2.6x baseline) for the gen-api cluster in us-west-2 starting ~2028-06-21T08:40:12Z. Throughput for a subset of customers dropped ~30% (requests queued/retried).

What we did immediately:
- Activated emergency routing to fallback model variant (gen-lite-v2) for affected routes (~08:46).
- Scaled the gen-api replica set by +30% for the routing tier (~08:50).
- Engaged kernel throttle to reduce long-tail token scheduling pressure for 10m windows.

Preliminary metrics attached (incident_snapshot.json) and screenshots (grafana-p95-spike.png).

Observed signals that look relevant:
- Large spike in KV cache miss rate at 08:39 which correlates with a routing policy change triggered by a partial node restart.
- Increased network retries between serving agents and router (5xxs on internal RPC).

Immediate ask: Need product + eng decision on customer-facing wording and whether to keep fallback routing for next 24h. Are we comfortable keeping gen-lite-v2 for affected tenants, or do we revert to primary once scaled capacity stabilizes?

Ben
Senior SRE
Redwood Inference

Attachments: incident_snapshot.json, grafana-p95-spike.png

Date: 2028-06-22T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Incident synthesis: P95 surge + routing exception — technical summary and proposed next steps

TL;DR: Root cause = brief routing daemon restart combined with an unexpected cache eviction pattern that created a KV miss storm; that, plus internal RPC retries, produced the P95 surge. Confidence: high.

What happened (short):
- At 08:39 a control-plane update caused a partial restart of the routing daemon on ~20% of nodes. On restart, routing policy re-evaluated sessions and forced cache invalidation in our prefix cache for some tenants.
- The cache miss storm created head-of-line token scheduling pressure and amplified tail latency.
- RPC retry storm between router and serving agents increased latencies further.

Immediate mitigations applied:
- Emergency routing to gen-lite-v2 (reduced p95 by ~60% for impacted requests).
- Temporarily disabled the new routing heuristic at 09:05 (this stopped additional nodes from invalidating caches).
- Increased node counts for serving tier and temporarily eased kernel throttle by 09:20.

Proposed next steps (timeline):
1) Short-term (next 6h): keep fallback routing enabled for impacted tenants, maintain hourly check-ins, and monitor p95 and KV miss rate (SRE).
2) Mitigation patch (24-48h): add safe-checks to routing-daemon startup to avoid mass cache invalidation; add retry backoff for internal RPC to prevent cascade. (Owners: Ops infra + Jonas).
3) Roadmap change (Q3): harden routing fallback logic, telemetry for cache invalidation events, and automated canary rollback triggers. (Owners: Product + Eng).

Customer messaging: here's a suggested short blurb we can send now — Chloe, please review and send if this matches product language.

--- CUSTOMER NOTE DRAFT ---

The mitigation reduced tail latency for impacted requests and we have disabled the new routing heuristic that was correlated with the event.

Our engineering team has identified the root cause and is deploying a short-term patch to prevent recurrence. We will follow up with a post-incident summary within 72 hours, including any customer-relevant findings about data fidelity and billing impacts. Please let us know if you need more frequent updates.

Best,
